title: Kagame Says International Sanctions Ignore Root Causes of DRC Crisis
detail: Rwanda's President Paul Kagame stated that international sanctions against Rwanda ignore the root causes of the DR Congo crisis, signaling continued friction between Kigali and the international community over the conflict's origins and blame attribution.

media.caption: Kagame says sanctions ignore the root causes of the DRC crisis

title: Kagame Accuses DRC of Arming and Integrating FDLR Fighters
detail: At the same Kigali news conference, President Kagame said Congolese authorities "are arming the FDLR and integrating its members into their own forces," citing testimony from former FDLR fighters as evidence, and said Rwanda's continued military involvement in eastern DRC was necessary self-defense: "if this problem is not resolved, it is natural for Rwanda to remain involved." Kinshasa has repeatedly countered that Kigali backs M23 with Rwandan troops, an allegation Rwanda denies.

media.caption: Kagame accuses DRC of arming and integrating FDLR fighters, Aug 25, 2026

confidenceReason: Kagame's accusation and the competing DRC/Rwanda narratives are both officially stated positions, not independently verified by UN or third-party sources.

title: Opposition Coalition C64 Announces Sept 15 March Against Constitutional Change
detail: The Coalition Article 64 (C64) — including Martin Fayulu, Jean-Marc Kabund, Moïse Katumbi, Augustin Matata and Delly Sesanga — announced on Aug 15 a nationwide peaceful march for Sept 15 opposing any revision of the 2006 constitution, particularly Articles 70 and 220, which it says could clear the way for a third Tshisekedi term. President Tshisekedi asked parliament on Aug 10 to reconsider the referendum law the Constitutional Court had approved in July; the National Assembly rescheduled deliberations for September. C64 said returning the bill to parliament was not a genuine retreat from the constitutional-change project.

media.caption: Demonstrators in Kinshasa protest the constitutional reform push, June 2026
